Subject: Reserved GPU commit — baseline metrics and measurement approach

Naomi — thanks again for the demo last week. The execs asked for a short write-up on two items before we move to commercial terms: (1) exact throughput commitments (tokens/sec and requests/sec) we can expect per committed GPU pool level, and (2) how Redwood will measure those metrics during onboarding and over the contract term (what tests, windowing, and tooling you use).

High level asks from our end:
- We want a guaranteed tokens/sec baseline (p50/p95) per 8xA100-equivalent pool.
- Clear latency target per request size (e.g., <= 150ms for 256-token responses at p95).
- Definition of measurement windows: warm vs cold runs, cache/kv usage, and what is included/excluded.

Can you send a short proposal we can attach to procurement? Also, curious whether guaranteed rate is stated as tokens/sec or as a blended requests/sec + token/sec rule.

Thanks,
Allegra

> Hi Allegra — great to hear from you. We can absolutely put a short, procurement-friendly doc together. I sketched the key points below and will loop in Karthik on the measurement specifics.
>
> Quick summary (proposal):
> - Commitment unit: reserved GPU pool expressed as N x 8xA100-equivalent devices. Guarantees are stated in tokens/sec per pool and a secondary requests/sec floor for small-response workloads.
> - Metric windows: rolling 5-minute and 1-hour windows for real-time SLA monitoring; monthly billing/credit computations use a 24-hour aggregated window with a 95th percentile (p95) computation.
> - Latency targets: per-request p95 targets by response-size buckets (<=64 tokens, <=256 tokens, >256 tokens). Example: 64-token p95 <= 80ms; 256-token p95 <= 150ms.
> - Measurement caveats: KV/prefix cache effects are included in production monitoring; we will provide a separate ‘cold-start’ benchmark run during onboarding (excluded from monthly billing credits).
>
> Attaching a draft SLA and the benchmark harness we propose to run during acceptance testing. Marcus will follow up on how we translate these guarantees into discount tiers.

> > Hi all — quick technical note to make the measurement definitions unambiguous for procurement and SREs.
> >
> > Measurement methodology (short):
> > 1) Tokens/sec definition: measured as total model-generated tokens divided by wall-clock time while the model is processing end-to-end requests (includes server-side tokenizer and response streaming overhead). For batch workloads, we report effective tokens/sec normalized to single-request concurrency (ex: 32 concurrent small requests -> effective token throughput computed as total tokens / wall clock).
> >
> > 2) Requests/sec floor: applicable for workloads where response token counts are <= 64 tokens. We compute rps as completed responses per second across a rolling 5-minute window; the contract will guarantee p95 rps >= X for a given commit band (we will specify X per commit level).
> >
> > 3) Latency targets: p95 latency measured end-to-end from first byte of request received to last byte of response sent. We will bucket by response size and by whether the request hit an active KV cache/prefix.
> >
> > 4) Acceptance tests vs ongoing SLA monitoring: Acceptance uses a controlled harness (attached) executed in your dedicated environment with synthetic traces reflective of your qps/tokendistribution. Production monitoring will use live telemetry; credits are computed on monthly aggregated p95 after excluding scheduled maintenance windows and a short onboarding warmup period (first 48 hours).
> >
> > Notes: we recommend committing on tokens/sec with a minimum rps floor. That gives predictable unit economics while protecting small-request workloads.
> >
> > I'll add the exact measurement commands and the harness invocation in the doc Naomi attached.
> >

> > > Hey Allegra — thanks for the clear ask. A couple of commercial clarifications so procurement has what they need:
> > >
> > > - Pricing bands: our standard commit tiers are 4/8/16 x 8xA100-equivalent. For each tier we publish an expected tokens/sec baseline and a guaranteed p95 floor.
> > > - Discounting: for a 12-month commit we can offer up to 18% off list for the 8-pool band (subject to final usage profile). Discounts scale with both commit size and term length; we anchor discount to measured utilization in months 2-4 and allow a one-time adjustment at month 6.
> > > - Credits: if actual p95 tokens/sec falls below the guaranteed floor in the billing month (excluding maintenance/warmup), we issue pro-rated service credits. The credit formula is in the attached SLA draft.
